metadata.source: N. Aiyaswami Shastri: Bhavasaṅkrānti Sūtra. Madras: Adyar Library, 1938, pp. 1-6.

body.text: 1. evaṃ mayā śrutam / ekasmin samaye bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati sma kalantakanivāse veṇuvane mahatā bhikṣusaṅaghena sārdhaṃ dviśatapacāśadbhiḥ bhikṣubhiḥ saṃbahulaiśca bodhisattvamahāsattvaiḥ / atha bhagavānanekaśatasahasraparivāraparivṛtaḥ purato 'valokya dharmaṃ deśayati sma / ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇamavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svarthaṃ suvyajanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ prakāśayati sma //
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>) was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove) at the <s>Kalantakanivāsa</s>, together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> — two hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s> — and with many <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas</s>. Then the Blessed One, surrounded by a retinue of many hundreds of thousands, looking before him, taught the <s>Dharma</s> — auspicious in the beginning, auspicious in the middle, auspicious at the end, of good meaning, well-expressed, complete, perfect, pure, and stainless — and set forth the holy life (<s>brahmacaryā</s>).

body.text: 2. tadā magadharājaḥ śreṇyo vimvisāraḥ mahātā rājavibhavena mahatā ca rājabalena rājagṛhānmahānagarānniṣkramya yena veṇuvanaṃ yena ca bhagavān tenopasaṅakramīt / upasaṅakramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā abhivandya triḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya ekānte atiṣṭhat / ekānte sthitvā magadharājaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ bhagavantametadavocat / kathaṃ bhagavan kṛtaṃ karma saṃcayaṃ pratirudhya ciraniruddhaṃ maraṇakāla upasthitaṃ manaso 'bhimukhībhavati / sūnyeṣu sarvasaṃskāreṣu kathaṃ karmaṇāmavipraṇāśo 'sti //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>, the king of <s>Magadha</s>, with great royal splendor and great royal power, going forth from the great city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, approached the <s>Veṇuvana</s> and the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One, circumambulated him three times, and stood to one side. Standing to one side, King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: "O Blessed One, how does accumulated <s>karma</s> (action), having been blocked and long since ceased, come to the forefront of the mind when the time of death arrives? When all <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) are empty, how is there non-destruction of <s>karmas</s>?"

body.text: 3. evamukte bhagavān magadharājaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisārametadavocat / tadyathā mahārāja puruṣaḥ suptaḥ svapne janapadakalyāṇyā striyā sārdhaṃ paricaret / sa śayitavibuddhaḥ janapadakalyāṇīṃ tāṃ striyamanusmaret / tatkiṃ manyase mahārāja svapne sā janapadakalyāṇī strī //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the Blessed One spoke to King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>: "Suppose, O great king, a man who is asleep consorts in a dream with a woman who is the beauty of the land. Upon awakening from sleep, he would remember that woman, the beauty of the land. What do you think, great king — does that woman, the beauty of the land, exist in the dream?"
He replied: "No indeed, O Blessed One."

body.text: 5. bhagavānāha!tat kiṃ manyase mahārāja api nu sa puruṣaḥ kiṃ paṇḍitajātīyo bhavet / yaḥ svapne janapadakalyāṇīṃ striyamabhiniviśet //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "What do you think, great king — would that man be of a wise nature, who would cling to the woman, the beauty of the land, in the dream?"

body.text: 6. āha! nohīdaṃ bhagavan! tatkasya hetoḥ / atyantatayā tu bhagavan svapne janapadakalyāṇī strī na saṃvidyate / nopalabhyate / kutaḥ punaranayāsārdhaṃ paricaraṇā / evaṃ vighātasya klamathasya bhāgī syāt //
body.translated_text: He replied: "No indeed, O Blessed One. For what reason? Because, O Blessed One, in the dream the woman, the beauty of the land, utterly does not exist and is not found — how much less could there be consorting with her? Thus he would be a partaker of exhaustion and fatigue [for nothing]."

body.text: 7. bhagavānāha!evameva mahārāja balo 'śrutavān pṛthagjanaścakṣuṣā rūpāṇi ddaṣṭvā saumanasyasthānīyāni rūpāṇyabhiniviśet / abhiniviṣṭa anurajyate / anuraktaḥ saṃrajyate / saṃrakto rāgajaṃ dveṣajaṃ mohajaṃ karma kāyavāṅmanobhirabhisaṃskaroti / tacca karma abhisaṃskṛtaṃ nirudhyate / niruddhaṃ na pūrvāṃ diśaṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati / na dakṣiṇām / na paścimām / nottarām / nordhvam / nādhaḥ / na vidiśaṃ niśritya tiṣṭhati / tat karma kadācinmaraṇa kālasamaya upasthite tatsabhāgasya karmaṇaḥ kṣayāt caramavijñāne niruddhe manaso 'bhimukhībhavati / tadyathāpi nāma suptaśayitavibuddhasya janapadakalyāṇi strī / evam hi mahārāja caramavijñānaṃ nirudhyate / aupapattyaṃśikaṃ prathamavijñānaṃ utpadyate / yadi vā deve / yadi vā mānuṣe / yadi vāsure / yadi vā narakeṣu / yadi vā tiryagyoniṣu / yadi vā preteṣu /
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: "Just so, great king, a foolish, unlearned ordinary person, having seen forms with the eye — forms that occasion pleasant feeling — clings to them. Having clung, he becomes attracted. Being attracted, he becomes attached. Being attached, he generates <s>karma</s> born of desire, born of hatred, born of delusion, through body, speech, and mind. And that <s>karma</s>, having been generated, ceases. Having ceased, it does not abide resting in the eastern direction, nor in the southern, nor in the western, nor in the northern, nor above, nor below, nor in any intermediate direction. That <s>karma</s>, at some time when the moment of death arrives, upon the exhaustion of similar <s>karma</s>, when the final consciousness (<s>caramavijñāna</s>) has ceased, comes to the forefront of the mind — just as the woman, the beauty of the land, [appears] to one who has awakened from sleep. Thus, great king, the final consciousness ceases, and the first consciousness of the new birth (<s>aupapattyaṃśika prathamavijñāna</s>) arises — whether among the gods, or among humans, or among <s>asuras</s>, or in the hells, or among animals, or among hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>)."

body.text:
tasya ca mahārāja prathamavijñānasya samanantaraniraddhasya tatsabhāgā cittasaṃtatiḥ pravartate / yatra vipākasya pratisaṃvedanā prajñāyate / tatra mahārāja na kaściddharmaḥ asmāt lokātparalokaṃ saṅkrāmati / cyutyupapattī ca prajñāyete / tatra mahārāja yaścaramavijñānasya nirodhaḥ / sā cyutiriti saṃjñā / yaḥ prathamavijñānasya prādurbhāvaḥ / sopapattiriti / caramavijñānaṃ mahārāja nirodhe 'pi na svacidgacchati / aupapattyaṃśikaṃ prathamavijñānamutpāde 'pi na kutaścidāgacchati / tat kasya hetoḥ /
svabhāvarahitatvāt / tatra mahārāja caramavijñānaṃ caramavijñānena śūnyam / cyutiścayutyā śūnyā / karma karmaṇā śūnyam / prathamavijñānaṃ prathamavijñānena śūnyam / upapattirupapattyā śūnyā / karmaṇāmavipraṇāśaścaprajñāyate / prathamavijñānasya mahārāja aupapattyaṃśikasya samanantaraniruddhasya nirantarā cittasantatiḥ pravartate / yatra vipākasya pratisaṃvedanī prajñāyate / evaṃ bhagavānāha / sugata evamuktvā anyadevamavocat śāstā //
body.translated_text:
O great king, immediately after the cessation of that first consciousness, a mind-stream of similar type proceeds, in which the experience of the ripening [of <s>karma</s>] is discerned. In this regard, O great king, no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever transmigrates from this world to the next world; yet death and rebirth are discerned. O great king, the cessation of the last consciousness — that is designated as 'death.' The manifestation of the first consciousness — that is 'rebirth.' O great king, the last consciousness, even in ceasing, does not go anywhere. The first consciousness pertaining to rebirth, even in arising, does not come from anywhere. For what reason?
Because it is devoid of inherent nature. O great king, the last consciousness is empty of the last consciousness. Death is empty of death. <s>Karma</s> (action) is empty of <s>karma</s>. The first consciousness is empty of the first consciousness. Rebirth is empty of rebirth. Yet the non-destruction of <s>karmas</s> is also discerned. O great king, immediately after the cessation of the first consciousness pertaining to rebirth, an uninterrupted mind-stream proceeds, in which the experience of the ripening [of <s>karma</s>] is discerned. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), the Teacher, spoke further:

children.translated_text: 8. All this is merely name, established upon mere designation;
apart from the designation, the designated [thing] is not found.

children.text: 9. yena yena hi nāmnā vai yo yo dharmo 'bhilapyate /
children.translated_text: 9. By whatever name whatsoever, whatever <s>dharma</s> is expressed,

children.text: nāsau saṃvidyate tatra dharmāṇāṃ sā hi dharmatā //
children.translated_text: that [dharma] is not found therein — this is the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>dharmas</s>.

children.text: 10. nāmnā hi nāmatā śūnyā nāmnā nāma na vidyate /
children.translated_text: 10. Name is empty of name-ness; name is not found through name;
all <s>dharmas</s> are nameless, yet they are illuminated through name.
11. These <s>dharmas</s>, being non-existent, are produced from conceptual construction;

children.text: sāpyatra kalpanā śūnyā yayā śūnyā vikalpitāḥ //
children.translated_text: and that very conceptual construction is itself empty — through which the empty [dharmas] are conceptualized.
12. That the eye sees form — what is called 'right seeing'
for the world that holds wrong belief — that is declared as <s>saṃvṛtisatya</s> (conventional truth).
13. Where the Guide explains that seeing [occurs] through the aggregate [of conditions],
the wise one declared that to be the ground of figurative expression of <s>paramārtha</s> (ultimate truth).

children.text: 14. na cakṣūḥ prekṣate rūpaṃ mano dharmānna vetti ca /
children.translated_text: 14. The eye does not perceive form, nor does the mind know <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: etattu paramaṃ satyaṃ yatra loko na gāhate //
children.translated_text: this is the supreme truth, which the world does not fathom.

body.text: 15. evamavocadbhagavān / magadhadeśarājaḥ śreṇyaḥ bimbisāraḥ te bodhisattvāste ca bhikṣavaḥ sadevamānuṣāsuragandharvaśca loko muditvā bhagavato bhāṣitamabhyanandan //
body.translated_text: 15. Thus spoke the Blessed One. The king of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>, those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, those <s>bhikṣus</s>, and the world with its <s>devas</s>, humans, <s>asuras</s>, and <s>gandharvas</s>, rejoicing, acclaimed the words of the Blessed One.
The Noble <s>Bhavasaṃkrānti</s> (Transmigration of Existence), a <s>Mahāyāna sūtra</s>, is complete.
